issue.title: How do you handle JavaScript errors?

repository.name: learn-rollup
repository.description: This is an example project to accompany a tutorial on using Rollup.

issue.body:
Right now if there is an error thrown in the JavaScript we've to restart the build process manually by running the npm script again. So if I manage to fix the error in my code, Rollup start compiling again. Is there away around this?

Sometimes when it tries to recompile again I get this error:

```sh
Maximum call stack size exceeded
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

Whenever this error pops up I've to restart the script again.

body:
I can also confirm this. Usually after getting an error it stops watching and sometimes it trigger this error afterwards:

```sh
Maximum call stack size exceeded
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

[This is my current rollup.config.js file.](https://gist.github.com/vinkla/ff162ea8f54daf0fca4af752272c0140)

issue.title: prevent mutation of cached ASTs
issue.body:
This fixes the dreaded 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' error that occurs with rollup-watch when a file with an error is subsequently fixed. It does so by preventing mutations of the cached AST, which is reused between incremental builds for files that *don't* have errors.

Fixes #1153, #1010, and https://github.com/rollup/rollup-watch/issues/21.

body: @Rich-Harris You are good man. very love you!

@Rich-Harris - #1205 didn't seem to solve the original issue here for me.  If rollup (or a plugin for rollup) encounters an error, I don't get the Maximum call stack size exceeded error, but once I fix the code issue, rollup doesn't attempt to recompile either, but the watch process is still running.  I have to stop the watch and restart it for it to recompile and continue watching for changes.
Anyone still watching this bug: it seems rollup/rollup-watch#38 is the real problem at this point.
